question: A researcher pastes a forty-page methodology handbook into a project's instructions field instead of uploading it as a document. What is the greatest concern with doing this?
options: A) Uploading is the only supported route, so pasting the handbook prevents the project from being saved at all.
B) Pasted text in the instructions is treated as a one-off prompt and is discarded when that chat ends.
C) The instructions become a document rather than direction, so the real house rules are buried and applied unevenly.
D) Project instructions can be read only by their author, so teammates in the project receive a different set of rules.
correct_answers: C) The instructions become a document rather than direction, so the real house rules are buried and applied unevenly.
explanations: Text can be typed into the instructions field; the problem is judgment, not a hard block.
Project instructions persist across chats; they are not discarded at the end of a conversation.
Correct. Instructions are for concise standing direction; burying a handful of rules inside long reference text weakens them.
Instructions belong to the project, and members with access see the same ones.
